pr_title: Change query to store host system info values
pr_body:
##### Summary
<!--
Describe the change in summary section, including rationale and design decisions.
Include "Fixes #nnn" if you are fixing an existing issue.
-->

Fixes #15271 
Fixes #15273 

This PR changes slightly how to store the host system info values. It uses inserts with binds, which will address the issue of the values having characters like `'`. Indeed though this will do multiple inserts instead of one, but since they are done once on start it shouldn't be much of an issue.

##### Test Plan

<!--
Provide enough detail so that your reviewer can understand which test cases you
have covered, and recreate them if necessary. If our CI covers sufficient tests, then state which tests cover the change.
-->

Change something in your `/etc/os-release`, i.e. put the value `NAME="'my_favorite_os'"`. Without this PR there will be fails to store this information. The table `host_info` would be empty (on a new agent). With this PR it should store the data.

2. Set up a Xen Server running XCP-ng 8.2.1 and ensure that netdata 1.19 is installed and running.

comments:
I see the error and it looks like it the database either doesn't like capital letters or doesn't like the hyphen, as its complaining about XCP and that only appears once in **NETDATA_HOST_OS_NAME**
```
2023-07-03 14:26:54: netdata ERROR : LIBUV_WORKER : Failed to execute 'INSERT OR REPLACE INTO host_info (host_id, system_key, system_value, date_created) VALUES (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_CONTAINER_OS_DETECTION','/etc/os-release', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_HOST_OS_NAME',''XCP-ng'', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_HOST_OS_ID','xenenterprise', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_HOST_OS_ID_LIKE','centos rhel fedora', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_HOST_OS_VERSION','8.2.1', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_HOST_OS_VERSION_ID','8.2.1', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_HOST_OS_DETECTION','/etc/os-release', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_SYSTEM_KERNEL_NAME','Linux', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_SYSTEM_KERNEL_VERSION','4.19.0 1', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE','x86_64', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_SYSTEM_VIRTUALIZATION','none', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_SYSTEM_VIRT_DETECTION','systemd-detect-virt', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_SYSTEM_CONTAINER','none', unixepoch()), (u2h('ba4f8972-25a1-11eb-88a9-ac1f6b9e03f2'), 'NETDATA_SYSTEM_CONTAINER_DETECTION','systemd-detect-virt', unixepoch())', rc = 1 (near "XCP": syntax error) -- attempt 0
2023-07-03 14:26:54: netdata ERROR : LIBUV_WORKER : METADATA: 'host:server01': Failed to store host updated information in the database
```

As it happens, MrZammler's patch didn't fix the problem I reported (but I'm sure that it fixed other issues) so I started digging around.
XCP-ng ships with a very old version of netdata and that version includes a plugin called system-info.sh (located at /usr/libexec/netdata/plugins.d/system-info.sh).
This includes the line
`echo "NETDATA_SYSTEM_OS_NAME=\"${NAME}\""`
This was modified to remove the escaped double quotes in a later version.
I made the same change on our XCP-ng servers and the problem went away.
@mjksohonet consider using the [latest stable version](https://learn.netdata.cloud/docs/installing/). Netdata v1.19 is old and has no support.

@ilyam8 we have a number of hypervisors running XCP-ng 8.2, this ships with, what appears to be, a customised version of Netdata v1.19 and we would be reluctant to change that.
The original objective was to get the metrics from the Xen servers into graphite but we discovered that the netdata app on the servers doesn't support exporting  directly to graphite.
This led to the decision to build a netdata 'relay' (currently running 1.40.1 ) that would collate the metrics and export them to graphite.
That process is working quite well, especially after we 'pruned' the metrics we didn't need to collect.

> we have a number of hypervisors running XCP-ng 8.2, this ships with

I'd suggest uninstalling v1.19 and switching to (for example) static build and keeping it up to date.

> we would be reluctant to change that

Why?

To put it simply, 'it ain't broke!'.
We're getting the metrics we want and now it's on to the rest of the backlog.

Actually, it is. See https://github.com/netdata/netdata/security/advisories. Additionally, there are a lot of improvements in all areas (much more reliable streaming, streaming compression, memory management, etc).
@ilyam8 While I do agree with you, the Xen-ng OS package appears to be a custom build of Netdata and we also don't want to mess with a hypervisor installed packages.
